findings.reason: §4 and §7 sequence the caller node first and base its 7.0 h on a launcher-plus-recording build; extending the existing header owner reduces it to setting two headers the receipts already parse.
findings.text: §4 ("The channel already exists, and it already carries a constant") proposes making the launcher stamp a declared identity into `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, a new transport for caller identity; but `identity_from_headers` at :111 already reads two dedicated headers, `x-reckon-run-id` and `x-reckon-session`, into `RequestReceipt.run_id` and `coordinator_session`, and §9-rewired already consumes `run_id` from that channel (97% of recent rows). §4 also still lists "No request receipt has ever been written" as a blocker, which §9-rewired's 2026-09-26 relay restart supersedes.

findings.reason: an unbounded second fork of the same call is a second owner for job liveness whose distinguishing failure is silent.
findings.text: the retention liveness probe forks its own `squeue` subprocess with no timeout and cannot tell an absent `squeue` from one that refused, duplicating the bounded owner `run_capture` (`node_probe.py:186`) and `read_jobs` (`node_probe.py:667`); already recorded at `c-20261005T1005-s8-plan-review` — extend that owner rather than the probe.

findings.reason: two aggregates over one window are two owners of one figure and can disagree.
findings.text: f-srw-020's proposed hourly rollup re-derives a per-window aggregate that `compact_rows` (`telemetry_store.py:596`) already writes as the hour tier; already recorded at `c-20261005T1005-s5-plan-review` — the node must extend the hour tier, or state in the followup why the tier cannot answer a long window.

findings.reason: the section adds CLI surface (§11 names its retirements; §8 does not) and the budget rule requires the section to name one or state why none exists.
findings.text: §8 rule 4 adds a retention command and a second run with an explicit apply flag without naming, in the section's own text, what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; the interface counts read `cli_options` 0, so a new option family must say what it replaces.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the store has one read path that selects exactly one tier per job (§8 rule 1), and §6's query surface is answered from that rather than reimplemented per consumer; no section hides the work behind a shallower module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: finding — §4 builds a second caller-identity transport where one already exists (first finding below); two further records remain open against owners in `telemetry_retention.py` and `telemetry_store.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: finding — §8's retention command adds a CLI surface without naming what it retires or merges; §11, by contrast, states its retirements in its own text, which is the pattern §8 needs.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every design section is grounded in cited code (the request-receipt fields in §4, the shared run predicate `telemetry_index.py:694` in §8, `telemetry_store.py:596` in §5, `node_probe` in §8), so prior art was searched rather than assumed absent; the one existing owner the search did not surface is recorded under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §11's `live_panel.py` computes the per-stream rate, the null-window rule and document staleness in the module itself and is explicitly not a passthrough; the `lane` block copies the router's own fields by design, which is the correct depth for a value another component already owns.
